## NotCapableError class

Thrown when an operation requires a backend capability (e.g. presence-per-use) that the active backend cannot provide.

**Signature:**

```typescript
declare class NotCapableError extends VaultError 
```
**Extends:** [VaultError](./vaultkeeper.vaulterror.md)

## Remarks

This is a configuration/backend mismatch, not a runtime authorization failure: the requirement was asserted against a backend whose configured instance does not advertise the capability, so no credential, session, or device is ever touched before this is thrown. It is fixable by switching to (or reconfiguring) a backend that provides the capability — inspect [NotCapableError.capability](./vaultkeeper.notcapableerror.capability.md) for which one was required and [NotCapableError.backendType](./vaultkeeper.notcapableerror.backendtype.md) for the backend that lacked it. Distinct from [AuthorizationDeniedError](./vaultkeeper.authorizationdeniederror.md) (a human/token rejection) and [PresenceDeclinedError](./vaultkeeper.presencedeclinederror.md) (a human declined a fresh action).
